title: Replication across populations and languages
rationale: The source found a misinformation sharing penalty of −18.2 points and a fact-check penalty of −13.3 points, but only among US Latino adults. The penalty looked smaller among Spanish-language respondents (−14.4 vs −20.1), and that gap is confounded with sample. This design runs the same headline-type randomization in white, Black and Latino adults, with Latino adults split by survey language.
contribution: Tests whether the information-type penalty and the trust gradient generalize across racial/ethnic groups and survey languages.
limitations: Forced-choice sharing is not real sharing behavior.
Survey language is self-selected by Latino respondents, so the language contrast is not causal.
Sharer attributes remain measured, not randomized, so the trust gradient is descriptive.
Headline wording may translate imperfectly into Spanish.

design.title: Headline type effects on sharing across population groups and languages
design.overview: Adults from matched YouGov samples (white, Black, Latino-English, Latino-Spanish) rate a contact, then complete paired-headline trials with randomized headline type. Population group is a measured stratum, and headline type is randomized within it. The outcomes are the source study's.
design.hypothesis: The misinformation sharing penalty is negative in all groups, and it is smaller among Spanish-language Latino respondents than among English-language Latino respondents. High sharer trust is associated with more sharing in all groups.
design.primaryOutcome: Chosen to share (1 if the headline was chosen in 'Which post would you be more likely to share?')
design.comparison: Misinformation vs true/neutral headline, with the information-type by group and by language interaction tested. The fact-check vs true/neutral contrast is secondary.
design.population: US adults in YouGov samples: white, Black and Latino (English or Spanish survey language), matched on age, gender and education.

assumptions: Power: about 1,500 respondents per group-by-arm cell gives an MDE near 0.04 at 80% power, given the language gap of 0.057 (−0.201 vs −0.144) with SEs near 0.014–0.020.
Four groups (white, Black, Latino-English, Latino-Spanish) times 3 arms is 12 cells, so about 18,000 respondents.
Platform is YouGov, with the survey offered in English and Spanish.
Group is a pre-treatment stratum, with randomization within strata and clustering at respondent level.
Outcomes and registered moderators are unchanged from the source study.
unresolved: The actual headline pairs (17 topics) and their Spanish translations must be supplied by the research team to replace the cond_note text.
Compensation, IRB number and the panel quotas must be set by the research team.
